# Benchmark — validation split

Run 2026-11-06T11:11:30+00:00 against `corpus_v1`, extractor `pdf_text:v1`. 40 documents.

**Synthetic data.** Every document was generated by `data/generate_corpus.py` from a seeded payload, which is the ground truth. Figures describe this corpus and nothing else.

## Extraction

| Measure | Familiar layouts | Unseen layout |
|---|---|---|
| Layout identified | 40/40 (100%) | n/a |
| Critical-field document accuracy | 40/40 (100%) | n/a |

Values invented on the unseen layout: **0**. Reading nothing from an unfamiliar document is the designed behaviour; reading the wrong label into a total is not.

## Pipeline conformance

40/40 (100%) of documents reached the state and exception codes they are labelled with.

This is a specification test: it says the implementation matches its own rules. It is not evidence that the rules are the right ones.

## Fault detection

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Recall over **all** seeded faults | 21/22 (95%) |
| Recall over faults a rule targets | 21/21 (100%) |
| Recall over faults no rule targets | 0/1 (0%) |
| Precision | 21/21 (100%) |

Of the undetectable faults that were flagged, **0** were flagged only because the document's layout could not be read, so every field was reported missing. That is not detection of the seeded fault and should not be read as such.

The corpus seeds faults the rules cannot catch on purpose — a supplier name that disagrees with a correct code, an invoice dated next year, a zero-quantity line, a line entered twice. The first row is the honest recall; the second is what the rules were built for; the third is the blind spot, and it should read zero.

## What this does not establish

- Synthetic documents from one generator. Real supplier invoices vary in ways a generator does not anticipate.
- Digitally generated PDFs with a text layer. No scans, no OCR.
- No timing, no cost, no comparison with doing the work by hand.
